THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Freezer Shortcut Beef Kebab Pitas

Freezer shortcut. 20 min end-to-end. One quick cook, two age-appropriate presentations. Adult: loaded pita with quick tzatziki + Shuug harissa (~400 cal / 30g protein). Kid: deconstructed tray with hummus in place of hot sauce. Frozen garlic is the no-waste hack; frozen fully-cooked kebabs skip the raw-meat prep entirely.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME20 min (10 min tzatziki + 8 min air fry + 2 min assemble)
COOK METHODAir fryer · Assembly
EST. / SERVING~400 cal | ~30g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: THAW THE KEBABS OVERNIGHT in the sealed pouch in the fridge. Cooking from frozen extends time + creates uneven heat.

Ingredients

PROTEIN

  • 6 fully cooked Mediterranean beef kebabs (keep 2 more available for hungry kids — 8 total from a 24 oz Costco pack)

QUICK TZATZIKI

  • 1 small 5.3 oz / 150g container plain 0% Greek yogurt
  • 1/2 cucumber, shredded and squeezed VERY dry
  • 3-4 cloves' worth frozen garlic, thawed
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • Salt, to taste

ADULT FINISH

  • Shuug Original Harissa Hot Sauce, to taste

CARB

  • 4 pita breads

SHARED FRESH

  • ~2 cups shredded iceberg lettuce
  • ~1 cup halved cherry / grape tomatoes
  • ~1/3 cup pickled red onions

COOKING

  • Avocado oil spray (kebab air-fry + pita warm)

Option 1

  • ~2 tbsp prepared hummus per kid (sub tzatziki if the kid likes it; adult tray works either way)
  • (NO Shuug — adult-only)

Allergens: gluten, dairy, sesame. Verify halal package Verify soy free package Verify nut free package

AT THE PLATE. Same kebab cook (all 6-8 kebabs air-fried together), same tzatziki (adults use it in the pita; kids skip it in favor of hummus), same vegetables (adults load into the pita; kids get on the tray). Presentation forks after the air fryer.

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.THAW. Thaw the sealed kebab pouch overnight in the fridge (do this the night before — day-of shortcut works for the tzatziki and assembly, not for the frozen protein).
  2. 2.TZATZIKI — YOGURT. Empty the 5.3 oz Greek yogurt container into a bowl.
  3. 3.TZATZIKI — CUCUMBER. Shred 1/2 cucumber, salt lightly, wait 5 min, then wring VERY dry in a clean tea towel. Add to the yogurt.
  4. 4.TZATZIKI — LEMON + GARLIC. Add 1 tbsp lemon juice + 3-4 frozen garlic cubes (thawed) + salt to taste.
  5. 5.TZATZIKI — MIX. Stir until thick and evenly combined. Refrigerate until plating.
  6. 6.AIR FRY THE KEBABS. Lightly mist the (thawed) kebabs with avocado oil and air fry 7-8 min per the CURRENT PACKAGE TEMPERATURE (physical package = source of truth; brands vary). Kebabs should be thoroughly hot with a light char at 8 min.
  7. 7.WARM THE PITAS. Lightly mist and warm the pitas 20-30 sec per side (dry pan or air fryer). Cut 2 pitas into wedges for the kids' trays.

Adult — Loaded Pita with Tzatziki + Shuug

  1. 8.BUILD THE ADULT PITA. Warm pita → generous smear of tzatziki → shredded iceberg → halved cherry tomatoes → pickled red onion → 2 air-fried beef kebabs → drizzle of Shuug to taste. Half-fold and eat immediately.

Kid — Deconstructed Tray with Hummus (No Shuug) · Option 1

  1. 8.BUILD THE KID TRAY. Warmed pita cut into wedges → shredded iceberg → halved cherry tomatoes → ~2 tbsp hummus in a separate compartment → 1 kebab to the side. Offer a second kebab per appetite.
  2. 9.OFFER MORE ON HUNGER. Keep 2 more warm kebabs available (8 total from the 24 oz Costco pack) in case kids want seconds. The photographed 7-year-old asked for a second — real appetite data.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult — Loaded Pita with Tzatziki + Shuug: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid — Deconstructed Tray with Hummus (No Shuug): Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • SQUEEZE THE CUCUMBER VERY DRY. Shred, salt lightly, wait 5 min, then wring in a clean tea towel until no more liquid comes out. This is the difference between thick tzatziki and runny sauce.
  • AIR FRY 7-8 MIN per the current package temperature — the physical package takes priority over any general guidance here (kebab brands and formulations change; the package is source of truth).

If something fails

Tzatziki is runny: Cucumber wasn't squeezed dry enough. Salt the shredded cucumber lightly, wait 5 min, then wring in a clean tea towel until no more liquid comes out. If already mixed, strain the tzatziki through a fine-mesh sieve or fold in 2 tbsp more Greek yogurt to thicken.

Kebabs came out dry or tough: Cooked from frozen (skipped the overnight thaw) or air-fried too long. Thaw the sealed pouch overnight in the fridge; check kebab temp at 7 min — brands vary. If already dry, top with extra tzatziki or a splash of olive oil to rehydrate.

Kid refuses the deconstructed tray: Try smaller portion sizes first — a few pita wedges + a spoonful of hummus + half a kebab + a couple tomatoes. Overloading the tray reads as pressure. Also verify the hummus isn't a strongly-flavored variety (roasted garlic / spicy) if kid is spice-sensitive.

Adult pita fell apart: Warmed pita too long or over-loaded the fillings. Warm just 20-30 seconds per side (dry pan or air fryer) — long enough to soften without drying out. Half-fold the pita around the kebabs rather than fully wrapping.

Not enough kebabs for hungry adults / kids: The recipe budget is 2 kebabs per adult + 1 per kid = 6 kebabs minimum. Keep 2 more available (8 total from the 24 oz Costco pack) for hungry eaters — the photographed 7-year-old asked for a second. Scale up per household appetite.

Shuug isn't available: Sub any harissa-forward hot sauce (Zab's, Mina, or NYShuk). Or use sriracha + a pinch of cumin for a warmer heat profile. Adult-only regardless of sub.

Hummus is bland for adult side: Add a swirl of olive oil + pinch of smoked paprika + squeeze of lemon on top of the hummus. Or use a flavored hummus (roasted red pepper, garlic, spicy) for the adult tray if you also want a hummus option there.

Storage and reheating

Store: Store tzatziki, vegetables, pita, hummus, and cooked/uncooked kebabs in separate sealed containers. Follow the kebab package for refrigerated storage and reheating guidance — the physical package is source of truth for storage temperature and shelf life.

Reheat: Kebabs: air fry 3-4 min from fridge to reheat, or per the package. Tzatziki: fold once, eat cold. Pita: 20-30 sec per side dry pan or 3-5 min at 300°F oven. Assemble immediately before eating for best texture.

Lasts: Tzatziki 3 days fridge. Cooked kebabs 2-3 days fridge per package. Pita 2-3 days room temp in a sealed bag, or freeze for longer. Pickled onions 2+ weeks fridge. Assemble pitas immediately before eating — pre-assembled pitas go soggy fast.

Estimated nutrition

~400 cal | ~30g protein.
